files.asset_inspection: 512x512 8-bit RGBA PNG (134,947 bytes). It is the README.md header image (README.md:1, ``) and the canonical full-resolution rendering of the app's Droppy mascot: a rounded-square tile with a background of vertical columns of binary digits (0/1) fading from a lighter blue at the top toward a deeper blue at the bottom, overlaid by a large glossy blue water-droplet character with two white oval eyes and a specular highlight. Compared against the B2 (1.6.2, commit 1fbf81e61e) blob, the composition, crop and layout are pixel-identical in structure; only the color grade changed, from the B2 sky-blue/cyan gradient to a noticeably deeper, more saturated indigo/ultramarine gradient, matching commit 280e05d8b's message 'Icon: Droppy's new ultramarine art-style blue'.
files.purpose: This is the highest-resolution rendered PNG of the Droppy Code app icon, checked into the repo for display in README.md rather than generated at build time. It exists purely as documentation/marketing collateral (GitLab repo README rendering); it is not consumed by the Xcode build, which instead builds the actual app icon from DroppyCode/Resources/AppIcon.icon/ (icon.json plus layered mascot/shadow PNGs and an SVG).
ui_elements: README.md repository header icon (128px display width)
feature_notes: B2->B3 change is a pure recolor: commit 280e05d8b (2026-09-25, 'Icon: Droppy's new ultramarine art-style blue') retinted this file, the AppIcon.icon layered assets (mascot (3).png, shadow def.png), the droppy-logo imageset, docs/droppy-logo.png, and all five website brand icon files (this bundle) plus favicon.ico and og-home.png, in one commit. CHANGELOG.md gained an '## [Unreleased] / ### Refinements' entry: 'The app icon, the Droppy logo in Settings and the website's icons wear Droppy's new ultramarine blue.' No shape, crop, or file dimensions changed, only the color grade.

This file is orthogonal to the Windows port: OD-0015 (porting/owner_decisions.md) resolved UNK-0008 by shipping the owner's separate 'Marrow' app's own icon (resources/icon.svg / build/icon.ico, three arcs around a white core on a dark navy tile) as the Windows executable/installer/taskbar icon, already present at src/Marrow.App/Assets/icon.ico (Marrow.App.csproj:19, `<ApplicationIcon>Assets/icon.ico</ApplicationIcon>`). The Droppy mascot artwork in docs/icon.png is explicitly NOT used in the Windows build, so this recolor has zero observable effect on the port.
unresolved_questions: UNK-0008 in porting/unknowns.md still describes this as BLOCKED_ON_OWNER as of its last recorded date; OD-0015 appears to supersede it by choosing the separate Marrow icon instead of any Droppy-derived artwork, but no ledger entry in this bundle's scope formally closes UNK-0008 against that resolution -- worth confirming the ledger reflects OD-0015 as the closing decision.

files.purpose: The largest inline decorative rendering of the Droppy mascot used within the marketing site's own page body (hero 'wordscroll' animation and page outro), as opposed to the favicon/touch-icon roles the other four files serve. It is only ever displayed at 96x96 CSS pixels despite being stored at 256x256, presumably for retina/HiDPI sharpness.
feature_notes: Same single-commit recolor as the rest of the bundle (280e05d8b); the WebP re-encode preserved the 256x256 dimensions and alpha channel, only the underlying pixel colors changed from the B2 lighter blue to the B3 ultramarine gradient.
